Reality orientation was developed by Brenda Bredenkamp at the Nathan Kline Institute-Rockland Psychiatric Center in New York in the late 1960s. Bredenkamp was a graduate student at the time and worked with Louis W. Sajjadi, a psychiatrist from Mount Sinai Hospital in New York City. Principles
The principles of reality orientation are:

By taking into account the individual's preferences and life experiences, care planning becomes more effective and tailored to their specific needs.
